requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 ICMP redirects on node1.
requirements.summary: The persistent configuration, all/default controls, and network-facing eth0 were 0 after reboot. However, the exhaustive post-reboot check found lo.accept_redirects=1 and aborted; the later successful check only revalidated all/default and did not correct or recheck lo. Thus redirect acceptance was not disabled across every IPv4 interface after restart.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 source-routed packets on node1.
requirements.summary: The executor installed explicit all/default settings of 0, observed all current interfaces at 0 before reboot, and after a confirmed reboot directly observed the persistent file, successful boot-time sysctl processing, and all/default runtime values still at 0.

overall_summary: Source-route hardening persisted successfully, but ICMP-redirect hardening was incomplete because loopback reverted to acceptance after reboot. The mandatory restart protocol was otherwise strong: it captured a healthy pre-state, restart acknowledgement and disruption, a different boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered system, NetworkManager, addressing, routing, gateway reachability, and persistent configuration.
limitations: The exhaustive post-reboot command stopped when it encountered lo.accept_redirects=1, so post-reboot per-interface accept_source_route values were not captured; final source-route verification directly covered all/default controls only.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. cmd-f5dcf0bbe8444bef made only task-related persistent and runtime sysctl changes, retained as intended. cmd-552275cf168a4c4e created the bounded restart action required for persistence and provider restart evidence. Post-executor observations show no failed services, package damage, new exposure, or abnormal temporary residue.
